The test image shows two tomato stems split lengthwise with their root systems exposed. Key features:
- Longitudinal stem cross-sections showing **brown internal discoloration** in vascular/pith tissue
- Root system appears decayed/brown
- No visible white mycelium, black sclerotia, or fluffy spores
- Stems show browning progressing from base upward

This strongly suggests vascular wilt disease. The brown vascular discoloration in split stems is a hallmark of **Verticillium Wilt**. Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference image shows classic Verticillium Wilt leaf symptoms (V-shaped brown necrotic lesion with yellow border). The test image shows stem/root symptoms of the same disease: internal brown vascular discoloration visible in the split stems, which the KB describes as "brown vascular discoloration visible when stems are cut lengthwise." The decayed roots and base browning are also consistent with Verticillium Wilt.

No white mycelium (rules out Southern Blight, Sclerotinia), no bacterial ooze evident (less likely Southern Bacterial Wilt), no dark cankers with concentric rings (rules out Alternaria).
